runtime_boundary_rules: Separate ECMAScript language core from browser APIs, Node APIs, tooling behavior, and Apps Script services.
Do not imply browser APIs are available in Node.
Do not imply Node APIs are available in browsers.
Do not imply Apps Script behaves exactly like browser or Node JavaScript.
Mark platform/tooling/security/deployment behavior current-verification-required unless official docs have been checked.
javascript_failure_mode_checklist: null/undefined before property access or destructuring
truthiness/defaulting with 0, empty string, false, null, undefined, NaN
implicit conversion in ==, relational comparison, +, arithmetic, template/string, JSON
shared object/array mutation and shallow copies
sparse arrays and array-like host collections
this binding in callbacks, methods, classes, event handlers
closure captured state and long-lived callbacks
prototype lookup, property ownership, descriptors, symbols, proxy traps
Promise rejection handling, await ordering, callback error paths, streams/workers/events
JSON serialization loss, Date/timezone assumptions, regex overmatching
async_review_checklist: Does every Promise-returning call get returned, awaited, or intentionally reported as background work?
Which rejection paths are caught or rethrown?
Which async operations must finish before return/render/write/send?
Which independent operations should start before awaiting?
Which callback APIs have error channels?
Which event/stream/worker lifecycle signals prove completion or failure?
Does async/await change a public API by returning Promise?
mutation_refactor_checklist: List mutating methods and property writes.
Distinguish binding immutability from object immutability.
Check shallow copy versus nested object sharing.
Add aliasing tests before changing mutation style.
module_system_checklist: Identify CommonJS, ES module, browser script/module, bundler transform, or test loader.
Check package.json type/exports and file extension.
Treat module conversion as behavior change because strict mode, top-level scope, and loader behavior can change.

browser: document/window/DOM/events/browser storage/browser networking/workers are browser host APIs.
apps_script: Apps Script server .gs, HtmlService browser HTML, triggers, services, quotas, scopes, uploads, and deployment are operational extension topics requiring current Google docs.

current_verification_rules: js-verify-google-apps-script: Google Apps Script runtime behavior

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Implicit coercion changes the value being compared or combined
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: A comparison, arithmetic operation, string concatenation, or truthiness check relies on JavaScript converting a value first.
failure_consequences: Numeric operation produces NaN or a string
Branch executes for a value the reader expected to be false
diagnostic_prompts: List every ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, +, Boolean(), if, ||, &&, ?? and template/string conversion site.
Check object-to-primitive hooks such as valueOf(), toString(), Symbol.toPrimitive when objects participate in operators.
preferred_mitigations: Prefer explicit conversion near the boundary.
Prefer ===/!== unless the loose comparison is intentional and documented.
Add tests for numeric strings, empty strings, 0, false, null, undefined, NaN, and objects.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Nullish value reaches property access or call
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: A variable may be null or undefined before a property read, element read, method call, destructuring step, or function invocation.
failure_consequences: Optional chaining hides a missing required value
Defaulting with || overwrites valid falsy values
diagnostic_prompts: Trace the first assignment and every branch that may return no object.
Ask whether missing, empty, null, undefined, and false are distinct states here.
preferred_mitigations: Use explicit guards or ?? defaults.
Use ?. only when absence is an accepted outcome.
Preserve distinction between null and undefined when APIs depend on it.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Mutation through shared object or array reference
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: Two variables, containers, closures, or modules point at the same object and one path mutates it.
failure_consequences: State changes appear far from the assignment site
Tests pass alone but fail in sequence
diagnostic_prompts: Identify which values are primitives and which are object references.
Find push/splice/sort/reverse/Object.assign/direct property writes.
preferred_mitigations: Clone intentionally when ownership changes.
Document mutating APIs.
Prefer returning new values for safe refactors unless performance or identity requires mutation.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Sparse array holes are treated like present elements
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: Code assumes every index below length has a value, but the array contains holes or deleted elements.
failure_consequences: JSON output changes holes to null
map/filter/forEach behavior differs from for/of or indexed loops
diagnostic_prompts: Check array creation with Array(n), delete, manual length changes, and out-of-range assignments.
Inspect whether method callbacks run for holes.
preferred_mitigations: Avoid sparse arrays for ordinary lists.
Initialize arrays explicitly.
Test Array(n), missing elements, and undefined elements separately.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Function depends on this but invocation loses receiver
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: A method is extracted, passed as a callback, or called through a different form so this is not the expected object.
failure_consequences: Writes land on wrong object in non-strict legacy code
Callback works as method but fails when passed directly
diagnostic_prompts: Identify every function using this and the exact invocation form.
Check arrow function versus function expression choice.
preferred_mitigations: Bind explicitly, wrap in a closure, or use an arrow only when lexical this is intended.
Avoid this-dependent callbacks unless the API documents receiver behavior.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Closure keeps state longer or differently than expected
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: A nested function captures variables by lexical scope, so later calls observe the captured variable state rather than a snapshot unless code creates one.
failure_consequences: Loop callback sees final or shared state
Tests fail when functions are reused
diagnostic_prompts: List variables captured by returned functions or callbacks.
Check whether the variable is reassigned after capture.
preferred_mitigations: Use block-scoped let/const for per-iteration bindings.
Pass values as parameters when snapshot semantics are needed.
Reset captured state deliberately in tests.

Prefer clear composition over opaque prototype tricks.

Store instants and local dates distinctly.
Test around midnight and DST changes.

top_reusable_risks.risk_name: Promise rejection has no reliable handling path
top_reusable_risks.plain_language_description: A Promise can reject and the code neither awaits it in a try/catch nor returns/catches it in the chain.
failure_consequences: Unhandled rejection warning or process policy action
Failure is lost while UI continues
Tests complete before async failure surfaces
diagnostic_prompts: Trace every Promise-returning call.
Check returned chains, await sites, catch/finally, and fire-and-forget comments.
preferred_mitigations: Return or await promises.
Catch at the boundary that can recover or report.
Test rejection paths.

workflow_playbooks.goal: Classify a file before making claims or edits.
inspection_steps: Identify runtime candidates from imports/globals/file path
Identify module system and top-level side effects
Mark host APIs and current-verification needs
Scan for high-risk constructs: coercion, nullish access, mutation, this, async, JSON/date/regex

workflow_playbooks.goal: Separate ECMAScript, browser, Node, Apps Script, and tooling assumptions.
inspection_steps: Map each file to runtime role
Check script tags or Apps Script file roles
Record current docs needed for platform behavior

workflow_playbooks.goal: Find coercion paths that affect comparisons, arithmetic, string output, truthiness, and JSON.
inspection_steps: Mark every boundary where strings/nullish values enter
Search operators == != < > <= >= + if && || ?? template literals JSON.stringify
tests_or_checks: Tests for "", "0", "10", 0, false, null, undefined, NaN, object operands

workflow_playbooks.goal: Prevent TypeError and hidden missing-data bugs.
inspection_steps: List nested access chains and destructuring sites
Decide required invariant versus optional absence
Add tests for missing parent and valid falsy child
tests_or_checks: Missing parent, null child, undefined property, 0/""/false values

workflow_playbooks.goal: Find aliasing and mutation that can break refactors or callers.
inspection_steps: Identify object/array parameters and module-level state
Search property writes and mutating methods
Distinguish shallow copies from deep ownership changes
Classify each mutating helper as intentional or bug
tests_or_checks: Original object unchanged or intentionally changed

workflow_playbooks.goal: Prevent receiver and captured-state bugs.
inspection_steps: Search this usage and classify invocation form
Check loop/block scoping and later mutation

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check inheritance, method placement, property ownership, and prototype lookup.
inspection_steps: Inspect own fields versus prototype methods

workflow_playbooks.goal: Ensure async work is awaited/returned, ordered, and failure-aware.
inspection_steps: Separate dependent sequential work from independent concurrent work
tests_or_checks: Assert function returns Promise where expected

workflow_playbooks.goal: Align thrown, rejected, emitted, callback, stream, and worker errors with the correct boundary.
Check DOM availability, element nullability, event propagation/defaults, and lifecycle.
Check network, HTTP, parse, stale-response, and environment-specific behavior.
inspection_steps: Separate network rejection from HTTP status
Check body parse and one-shot body use
Check credentials/CORS/security needs against current docs

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check client storage choice, sensitivity, quota/error handling, and current platform behavior.
Check Node-only file APIs, async error paths, streams, buffering, and deployment permissions.
inspection_steps: Verify code is not browser/App Script path
Choose stream vs buffered read by size

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check Node HTTP API boundaries, stream lifecycle, async errors, and deployment security.
inspection_steps: Check input validation and output serialization
Flag current Node/security docs where needed

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check message schemas, lifecycle, errors, transfer/copy, and security/deployment constraints.
inspection_steps: Check command injection/deployment permissions for child process

workflow_playbooks.workflow_name: Review Apps Script code as extension
workflow_playbooks.goal: Review Apps Script without pretending it is browser or Node JavaScript.
inspection_steps: Create file-role map: .gs server, HtmlService client HTML, shared/generated, local tooling
List Apps Script services, triggers, scopes, quotas, deployment behavior to verify
Check SpreadsheetApp read/write safety and idempotence
tests_or_checks: Small Apps Script probe where docs leave ambiguity

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check data conversion and text/time edge cases.
inspection_steps: List JSON value types and round-trip requirements

workflow_playbooks.goal: Check that lint/format/test/build tools support the actual JS runtime target.
inspection_steps: Inspect ESLint env/parser and ignored files
Compare tested code with deployed code

workflow_playbooks.goal: Plan a behavior-preserving change around JavaScript-specific risks.
inspection_steps: List semantics the refactor might change: coercion, nullish, mutation, this, closure, prototype, async, JSON/date/regex

workflow_playbooks.goal: Design a compact test set that targets actual JavaScript risks.
inspection_steps: Pick one happy path and one edge/failure path per relevant risk
Include async rejection and ordering when async exists
Include runtime smoke test when host boundary exists
Include JSON/date/regex edge cases where data crosses boundaries

inspection_steps: Ask whether behavior changed after 2020 or after model cutoff
Mark output as verification-required until checked
tests_or_checks: Official docs/release notes checked in downstream work

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use const for bindings that are not reassigned; use let for reassignment; leave var only when maintaining legacy scope behavior deliberately.
specific_checks: Check reassignment separately from object mutation

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use === and !==; use value == null only as an intentional null-or-undefined check when both are equivalent for that branch.
Use plain objects for fixed-shape records with known property names; use Map for dynamic keys, non-string keys, or collection semantics.
specific_checks: Check key types and serialization needs

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use arrays for ordered dense lists; use objects for named records.
specific_checks: Check whether order or names drive access

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use array for ordered lists where duplicates may matter; use Set for membership uniqueness and has/delete operations.
specific_checks: Test insertion order and membership semantics

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use the simplest representation: plain function for behavior, class for constructed objects with shared methods, closure for private state or specialization.
Use prototype/class methods for shared behavior; use instance functions/arrow fields only when per-instance closure state or lexical this is required.
Use the module system already required by the runtime/build/test/package boundary; do not mix formats in one file without verified interop.
Use the abstraction exposed by the underlying API; use async/await for sequential Promise flows; wrap callbacks only with tested error and multiple-settle behavior.
Use arrays for small reusable lists; use iterators/generators for lazy, potentially large, or custom traversal; use async iteration for values arriving over time.
Use regex for flat, regular, well-tested patterns; use a parser or manual scanner for nested, ambiguous, security-sensitive, or heavily escaped formats.
Use JSON for plain data; use custom serialization/schema when values include Date, Map, Set, Error, BigInt-like needs, cycles, classes, functions, symbols, or prototypes.
Use the smallest client storage mechanism that matches data sensitivity, size, lifetime, and current browser support after verification.
Keep simple UI work on main thread; use worker for CPU-heavy or blocking work that can be isolated behind messages.
specific_checks: Test worker error/termination and unsupported values

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use buffered read for known-small data; use streams/async iteration for large, unbounded, or incremental data.
Use worker threads for CPU-bound JavaScript that can communicate by messages; use child processes for trusted external commands or process isolation when deployment permits.
Run DOM/UI code in the browser; run filesystem/OS/server code in Node; keep shared logic free of host APIs.
Treat Apps Script as its own operational host; classify server .gs, HtmlService client HTML, triggers, and generated/local tooling separately.
specific_checks: Current Google docs for every service/trigger/quota/scope

decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Use native features when all target runtimes support them; use transpilation/polyfill only when build/test/deploy path is verified.
Use formatting for consistency, linting for suspicious patterns/environment rules, and tests for behavior; do not let any one tool stand in for the others.
specific_checks: Add tests for risks found in review

decision_shortcuts.decision_name: when not to use Proxy or metaprogramming
decision_shortcuts.default_low_complexity_choice: Do not use Proxy/metaprogramming for ordinary data flow. Use it only for a clear library/boundary problem with tests for traps and invariants.

ai_agent_response_standard: Start with runtime/module/source evidence when reviewing code.
Name concrete JavaScript behavior, not generic programming advice.
For each finding, include symptom, root-cause pattern, risk ID, diagnostic check, and minimal test when useful.
When current docs are required, say so instead of guessing.
For Apps Script, label the record as operational extension and verify Google docs before production claims.
